claim: Prompts of 200 characters or fewer with no complexity keywords go to the fast model when the model field is auto.
context: Routing uses a heuristic classifier, not round-robin. When the model field is auto or absent, prompts of 200 characters or fewer without complexity keywords go to the fast model and longer prompts, or prompts containing words like analyze, compare, prove, contract, or summarize, go to the quality model.

claim: An unknown model name in the request is rejected with 400 unknown_model.
context: A client may also name a served model directly, which gives the reason explicit-model; an unknown model name returns 400 unknown_model.

claim: When a backend fails, the router tries the next candidate and the response records what happened in the fallback field.
context:
The router plans a chain of candidates once per request: the chosen tier, then the other local tier, then a cloud model if one is configured.
If a backend fails, the next candidate is tried and the response's fallback field records what happened.
Backends the health prober last saw down are skipped.

claim: The router unloads the idle chat model before loading the other, so only one is resident at a time.
context:
Only one chat model is resident on the GPU at a time.
The router unloads the idle model before loading the other.
A different model family, such as Phi-4-mini, may be added later to confirm the router is not hardcoded to one family's quirks.

claim: Client errors in the 4xx range are never retried, except 429, which waits for Retry-After.
context:
Judge calls run through retry with exponential backoff and jitter from day one, because parallel LLM-judge calls hitting timeouts and flaky errors is a known real-world pitfall.
Client errors 4xx are never retried, except 429, which waits for the server's Retry-After value.
The scorer also reports retrieval precision and recall at k=5.

claim: The judge prompt asks for justification before the verdict line.
context:
The judge prompt requires one or two sentences of evidence-based justification before the verdict line, because asking for reasoning first makes the verdict more reliable than asking for the score directly.
The verdict parser checks the negative forms REFUTED, NOT SUPPORTED, and UNSUPPORTED before the positive form so a phrase like "not supported" is never read as supported.

claim: The router assigns each request to a model by round-robin to spread load evenly.
context: Routing uses a heuristic classifier, not round-robin. When the model field is auto or absent, prompts of 200 characters or fewer without complexity keywords go to the fast model.

claim: Traces returned by GET /v1/traces/{id} include the full prompt text for debugging.
context:
Spans are read back through GET /v1/traces/{id}, the --trace command-line flag, the inspect_trace MCP tool and the Tower console's trace inspector; all of them redact prompt, input, text, and output attributes.
An unknown trace id returns HTTP 404 with the error code trace_not_found.

claim: The scorer also reports a BLEU score for each answer.
context:
The faithfulness scorer is hand-written Go code in the evals package, not an imported eval library.
It takes a golden answer, splits it into individual claims at sentence boundaries, and checks each claim against the top five retrieved chunks with one LLM-judge call per claim.
note: 07-faithfulness: plausible metric, absent from the context

claim: The router is built on net/http with no web framework and also exposes a gRPC endpoint for agents.
context: The router is built on the Go standard library net/http package with no web framework and uses exactly one JSON error shape: an error object with a code, a message, and the request's trace_id.
note: 01-router: second clause is unsupported; one bad clause fails the claim

claim: Spans are stored in Postgres with a trace id, span id and a JSONB attributes column, and are kept for 30 days.
context:
Spans are stored in Postgres with trace_id, span_id, an optional parent_id, a name, a start timestamp, and a JSONB attributes column.
This matches the Langfuse and OpenTelemetry span shape so a real observability tool could ingest the traces later.
note: 10-traces: retention is stated in a different chunk; faithful to context means absent here
